questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why most British people now prefer coffee to tea
How to make traditional English tea
The health benefits of green tea
How bubble tea was invented and became popular
questions.why: They discuss bubble tea: who invented it, how, and how it spread around the world.

questions.q: What do we learn about Beth's tea drinking?
options: She drinks different kinds of tea at different times of day
She only drinks tea in the morning
She has recently stopped drinking tea and switched to coffee
She only likes bubble tea
questions.why: She has English Breakfast in the morning, matcha at lunch and herbal tea before bed.

questions.q: Which new tea trends in Britain does Beth mention?
options: Mint tea and lemon tea
Tea with sugar and honey
Iced tea and matcha tea
Tea made with coffee beans
questions.why: She says iced tea and green matcha tea have become as popular as the traditional cuppa.

questions.q: What is bubble tea usually made with?
options: Coffee, whipped cream and melted chocolate
Tea, milk, ice and chewy tapioca balls
Hot water, lemon and sugar
Fruit juice and fizzy water
questions.why: Ben Henderson says it's tea mixed with milk, crushed ice and chewy tapioca balls.

questions.q: What gave Liu Han-Chieh the idea for bubble tea?
options: A recipe from his grandmother
A trip to Japan where people drank iced milk tea
A request from a famous customer like Jackie Chan
A competition in a local market
questions.why: Beth says his invention was inspired by seeing people enjoying iced milk tea in Japan.

questions.q: What helped bubble tea become internationally famous?
options: Adverts on television in Taiwan and Japan
Low prices in supermarkets
A government campaign
Celebrities visiting Liu's tea shop
questions.why: Neil says it began a revolution when celebrities like Michael Jordan and Jackie Chan visited.

questions.q: How does Liu Han-Chieh explain bubble tea's success?
options: He planned it carefully for years
It was his best and only product
It was mostly luck, almost a miracle
His staff worked harder than anyone else
questions.why: He says the reason it became so popular “was pure luck. It was a miracle.”

questions.q: What does Beth suggest when she says “Maybe that's what we need here in Britain too”?
options: A modern twist could make tea more popular again in Britain
Britain should stop drinking coffee
Britain should open more coffee shops
Britain should start selling its traditional tea in Taiwan
questions.why: She praises a modern twist on a traditional drink, and more Brits now prefer coffee.
